meta.description: Tell Kept what you want to get better at. It writes you a plan, asks for one small promise a day, and checks in with you tomorrow.

plan.heading: Tell Kept a goal. Get a plan.
plan.support: You answer four short questions about your goal. Kept’s AI turns your answers into a plan in about 10 seconds. Here’s what it makes:

run.label: Running
run.promise: After work, I will walk and jog for 10 minutes.

cook.label: Cooking
cook.goal: Cook dinner at home most nights, in 4 weeks
cook.milestone: Week 2: cook 3 dinners in one week
cook.promise: After work, I will pick one recipe for tomorrow.
cook.idea: Decide what to eat before you’re hungry

guitar.label: Guitar
guitar.goal: Play 3 songs on the guitar, in 12 weeks
guitar.milestone: Week 4: switch between G, C and D without stopping
guitar.promise: Before bed, I will play one chord for two minutes.
guitar.idea: A little every day beats a lot once a week

plan.note: Every plan has 2 to 4 checkpoints, 3 to 5 daily actions that each come in a small, medium and large size, and 5 ideas that explain why they work. You can change it before you start.

about.heading: Why it’s called Kept.
about.lead: For centuries, people kept promises the same way: write it down, then check it off. Kept works like that. Each evening you write down one small promise. The next day you say whether you kept it.
about.second: Over the weeks, those answers add up to your record: what you kept, what you partly kept, and what slipped. No streaks to lose and no points to chase, just an honest account of what you did.
about.imageAlt: A ledger from the 1830s with a marbled green and gold cover
about.hoursAlt: A handwritten page of accounts from 1846, each job drawn in watercolour beside the hours it took and its price
about.hoursCaption: An account of hours spent, Paris, 1846. Every job entered, every hour counted.

what.q: What is Kept, in one sentence?
what.a: A two-minute daily check-in that turns a goal into one small promise a day, and helps you keep it.

goals.q: What kind of goal can I bring?
goals.a: Anything you want to get better at: running, cooking, an instrument, a language, sleep. Kept won’t plan anything unsafe, like a crash diet, and suggests a safer version instead.

dayOne.a: About five minutes. You answer four short questions: your goal, how many weeks to give it, where you are now, and what usually gets in the way. Kept writes your plan, you check it, and you make your first promise.

ai.a: Two things. It writes your plan from your answers, and it marks your answer when an idea comes back. It runs on GPT-6 Luna through OpenRouter, using only providers that don’t keep what you send, but don’t type anything private.

missed.q: What if I miss a day?
missed.a: It doesn’t count against you. A promise you don’t report by the end of the next day closes as unreported, and Kept doesn’t make your promises smaller because of it.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. Kept runs in your browser. At setup you add one daily reminder to your calendar, and it brings you back to the day’s check-in.

private.a: Only you see your goal, your plan and your answers. Our public results page shows totals across everyone testing Kept, with no names, emails or goals.

footer.credit: Ledger pictures: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain.
footer.legal: Plans are written by AI as general guidance, not medical, financial or legal advice.

familiar.heading: Sound familiar?
familiar.support: Most goals don’t fail because people don’t want them enough. They fail in the same few ways. Switch on the ones that sound like you.

fade.sentence: I start strong, then stop after a week.
fade.result: Kept starts you small, so day one is easy. It only asks for more after three Yeses in a row.

stuck.sentence: I never know what to actually do today.
stuck.result: Every evening you pick one small action for tomorrow, so you always know what’s next.

forget.sentence: I read the advice, then forget it.
forget.result: Kept brings each idea back 1, 3 and 7 days after you learn it and asks you about it, so it stays with you.

badDay.sentence: One bad day and I give up.
badDay.result: A missed day doesn’t count against you. Two Noes in a row and Kept makes your next promise smaller, not harder.

ResultsPage.heading: What our testers actually did.
ResultsPage.intro: Raw counts from everyone testing Kept, people who stopped included, updated about once a minute. They come from the same saved events as each person’s ledger. No names, emails or goals. The demo account and our own accounts aren’t counted.

checkingIn.heading: Still checking in
checkingIn.note: Testers who submitted a report on that day, counted from their own sign-up day. Day 1 is setup, so the first report comes on Day 2. The latest days can still go up.
checkingIn.empty: No tester has reached Day 2 yet.

promises.heading: Promises
